title: Birdfy Gifts for Backyard Birders: Top Smart Feeders After Two Years of Testing
content: Following over two years of testing smart bird feeders, the author shares recommended gifts for backyard birders. The selection includes a simple camera feeder and a nest box, which allowed the author to observe chickadees raising their young.
summary: I tested smart bird feeders for more than two years. The picks include a simple camera feeder and a nest box that lets me watch chickadees raise their young.
author: Wired

title: Pura fragrances 20% off, diffusers 30% off through Dec 6 for Cyber Week
content:
Pura offers special Cyber Week discounts: fragrances are 20 percent off and diffusers are 30 percent off, with the promotion running through December 6.  

After testing three generations of Pura devices, the writer shares which products they would choose during this sale.
summary: Pura fragrances are 20 percent off and diffusers are 30 percent off through December 6. The author recommends purchases after testing three generations of Pura devices.
author: Wired

title: Signal blocks Gemini and Siri AI from reading screen on iOS
content:
Signal has introduced a new privacy feature for its iOS users, giving them the ability to toggle a setting that blocks screenshots and prevents the Siri AI from scanning on‑screen content. The same restriction will also apply to Android devices, limiting the ability to capture screenshots of Signal conversations.

Signal’s president, Meredith Whittaker, explained in a recent blog post that the agentic AI capabilities built into operating systems—capable of analyzing on‑screen information—are undermining the company’s ability to guarantee privacy. She urged OS providers to give app developers more robust tools to control what data these AI agents can access.

Whittaker emphasized that this is a serious problem, noting that Signal and other application developers currently lack the necessary safeguards to prevent AI agents from reading user data.
summary: Signal has added an option for iOS users to block screenshots and stop Siri AI from scanning on-screen content. The company also restricts screenshot capability on Android and iOS to protect privacy from AI agents.
author: The Verge

title: Vergecast Discusses Week of Tech Outages, From Outlook to iCloud
content: There was a dayslong Outlook outage. A nationwide ground stop for only the second time in 25 years. Banks seemed to suddenly stop working. Even iCloud couldn't stay up and running. This week, it felt like the technological world simply collapsed. And it felt like this might be the beginning of something even bigger. On this episode of The Vergecast, Nilay and David go through the week's many calamities, and try to explain both what happened in each case - which was generally much milder than the conspiracy theories would have you believe - and why all these small issues might still add up to something worth worrying about. In a world filled …
summary: The episode covers a week of tech outages, including a dayslong Outlook outage, a nationwide ground stop, banks that suddenly stopped working, and an iCloud outage. Nilay and David explain each incident and argue that these small issues could add up to a larger problem.
author: The Verge

title: Grand Theft Auto VI Released: Rockstar Returns With Flexible Open-World Game
content:
Grand Theft Auto VI has finally entered the gaming world, marking a return for Rockstar after a 13‑year gap since GTA V and an eight‑year pause since Red Dead Redemption 2. The new title is described as a sprawling, extravagant open‑world experience that expands the franchise’s established formula.

The game’s design emphasizes flexibility, allowing players to shape their adventure. While the core of the series remains a “maniacal criminal” experience, GTA VI also offers a new love story element, highlighted by a dedicated button for holding hands. Players can choose to immerse themselves in romance, or pursue other activities.

Additional gameplay options include fishing and driving around the world while listening to the in‑game radio. These features illustrate the game’s broad appeal, catering to a wide range of play styles and interests.
summary: It's hard to believe, but Grand Theft Auto VI is now a real thing that we all can play. Thirteen years after GTA V, and eight years since Red Dead Redemption 2, Rockstar is back with its latest sprawling, extravagant open world.
author: The Verge

title: UN court finds Myanmar guilty of genocide, cites military Facebook posts
content: Rohingya refugees in Bangladesh watch the International Court of Justice’s ruling on Myanmar’s genocide against its Muslim minority. | Photo by Salahuddin Ahmed / AFP via Getty Images In its ruling that Myanmar committed state-sponsored genocide against the Rohingya people in 2016 and 2017, the United Nations' top court says that Facebook played a role in helping Myanmar's military spread hate speech against its Muslim minority. The ruling from the International Court of Justice determined that Facebook posts made by the country's military "dehumanized" the Muslim minority "and at times encouraged and legitimized violence against them," as reported earlier by Reuters. The decision that Myanmar committed genocide comes after The Gambia sued the country in 2019 over the military's violent "clearance operations" targeting t …
summary: The International Court of Justice ruled that Myanmar committed state-sponsored genocide against the Rohingya in 2016 and 2017. The court said Facebook posts by the military dehumanized the Rohingya and at times encouraged violence.
author: The Verge

title: Andrey Zvyagintsev says filmmakers, not executives, understand audience desires
content:
In 2022, Vladimir Putin announced a military draft that frames the backdrop of Andrey Zvyagintsev’s film Minotaur. The movie is set in the fictional town of Krasoborsk and follows a quietly unhappy couple, Gleb and Galina, as they try to maintain their lives amid the geopolitical climate.

Minotaur is a remake of Claude Chabrol’s 1969 film The Unfaithful Wife. In the story, Galina engages in an affair, shown through a scene of her texting with a faint smile while her face is lit by her phone. Gleb runs a private contracting concern and is soon asked to raise funds, adding tension to their domestic situation.
summary: Andrey Zvyagintsev argues that filmmakers are better at gauging what viewers want than studio executives. His 2022 film Minotaur, set in the fictional town of Krasoborsk during Putin’s draft announcement, follows a quietly unhappy couple, Gleb and Galina, as they navigate personal and geopolitical pressures.
author: The Verge

title: Trump admin ban blocks TP-Link's new Wi‑Fi 8 routers from US market
content:
TP‑Link, a leading supplier of wireless routers for U.S. homes and small businesses, is currently barred from selling its newest Wi‑Fi routers in the United States. The restriction stems from a ban the Trump administration instituted in March 2026 that blocks the import or sale of any new consumer router that is manufactured, assembled, designed, or developed outside the United States.

The administration controls exemptions through a waiver‑review process that involves the Federal Communications Commission, the Department of Defense and the Department of Homeland Security. While some competing manufacturers have secured such waivers, TP‑Link has not been granted one and its recent Wi‑Fi 8 models remain prohibited from U.S. import and sale. Routers that received approval before the March 2026 ban continue to be available in the market.
summary: TP-Link cannot sell its newly released Wi‑Fi 8 routers in the United States because the Trump administration's March 2026 ban on foreign-made consumer routers blocks import of new models without a waiver. Its routers approved before the ban remain available, but the company has not obtained an exemption unlike some competitors.
author: Ars Technica

title: Writer urges subscriptions to Ars Technica after 21 years with the site
content:
A writer for Ars Technica reflects on a 21‑year tenure with the site, noting that it has been the sole publication venue throughout their career and instrumental in their evolution from scientist to blogger to journalist. The author describes the role at Ars as uniquely independent, allowing both editing and writing responsibilities, and characterizes such positions as rare in journalism.

The piece serves as a personal appeal for readers to support Ars Technica through a subscription, emphasizing that continued financial backing would help preserve the writer’s current role. The author outlines three reasons to subscribe: the quality of the writing, the people involved, and the community that the site fosters. The full article and comments are available for further reading.
summary: The author notes it has been 21 years since their first article at Ars Technica and that the site has been their only writing home. They ask readers to support Ars Technica with a subscription, citing benefits of its writing, people, and community.
author: Ars Technica

title: Seminole Tribe sues DraftKings over illegal Florida online gambling offerings
content:
DraftKings has asked a federal court in Florida to assume control of a lawsuit that the Seminole Tribe recently filed against the company. The move adds a new front to the broader national debate over online “swaps” and prediction markets.

In the suit, the Seminole Tribe argues that two of DraftKings’ current online products—the fantasy‑sports‑style “Pick6” and the “Super App” sportsbook—are illegal under Florida law. The case highlights the complex landscape of Indigenous tribes, some of which are challenging prediction markets while others seek to participate in them.
summary: The Seminole Tribe, the only entity permitted to offer online gambling in Florida, has filed a lawsuit against DraftKings. The tribe says DraftKings’ “Pick6” fantasy‑sports product and its “Super App” sportsbook are illegal in Florida, and DraftKings has asked a federal court to take over the case.
author: Ars Technica

title: SpaceX recovers Starship stage, ULA's Vulcan fails; ICEYE pursues Avio; Stoke marks engine milestone
content:
Edition 9.20 of the Rocket Report highlighted a weekend that illustrated the divergent paths of two of America’s most experienced launch providers. On Saturday, SpaceX successfully performed a mid‑air capture of the Starship upper stage at its Texas launch pad after the vehicle spent nearly a day in orbit. The Super Heavy booster that powered the flight was lost at sea, but SpaceX noted that it has previously recovered that portion of the rocket on other flights, underscoring progress toward a fully reusable system.

In contrast, United Launch Alliance experienced its first total launch failure when the Vulcan rocket failed on its maiden flight. The failure affects not only ULA but also the U.S. Space Force and Amazon, both of which have booked roughly 70 Vulcan launches over the coming years.

The newsletter announced a brief pause for the Thanksgiving holiday, with the next issue slated for the first week of December, and invited readers to submit content and subscribe for future reports.

In European news, Finnish satellite developer ICEYE disclosed plans to acquire Italian rocket maker Avio for more than $2.2 billion, aiming to create Europe’s first vertically integrated end‑to‑end space company, according to Ars. Avio produces the Vega C solid‑fuel launcher, capable of delivering up to 3.3 metric tons to low‑Earth orbit. ICEYE’s most recent fundraising round in June valued the company at over $12 billion.
summary: Welcome to Edition 9.20 of the Rocket Report! Last weekend was a picture of the US launch business in miniature, and emblematic of the opposing trajectories of two of the nation's most experienced rocket makers.
author: Ars Technica

title: SpaceX lenders seek to block Musk from sending AI chip collateral into space
content:
Lenders that are financing SpaceX’s newest $43 billion debt package, which is secured by the company’s advanced AI chips, have moved to block Elon Musk from sending that collateral into orbit.  According to people familiar with the matter, the lenders are worried that if SpaceX were to launch the chips as part of Musk’s proposal for orbital data centers, they would be unable to recover and sell the semiconductors should a default occur.

Musk has outlined a plan to power AI models with data centers cooled by the vacuum of space, a concept that would involve loading satellites with the same advanced chips tied to the debt agreement.  SpaceX, however, has stated that the chips covered by the financing will be used on Earth, not placed aboard satellites.  The lenders’ objection centers on preserving their ability to reclaim the collateral if the loan terms are not met.
summary: SpaceX lenders seek to block Musk from sending AI chip collateral into space.
author: Ars Technica

title: US to announce root cause of FAA router outage causing nationwide ground stop
content:
The U.S. government will soon announce the root cause of the router outage that triggered the Federal Aviation Administration’s third‑ever nationwide ground stop. The outage forced roughly 3,500 aircraft to land immediately and affected more than 1 million passengers on the afternoon of Friday, November 13. That day saw over 12,000 flight cancellations, a figure that rose to more than 20,000 over the weekend as travelers sought accommodations and alternative transportation.

FAA Administrator Bryan Bedford told reporters that investigators are “very close” to determining the root cause, according to CNN. Bedford added that Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy plans to present the findings at a news conference as early as Friday, November 20. Questions remain about whether the FAA’s modernization of the national airspace system is being conducted with appropriate risk assessments and adequate oversight of private contractors.
summary: US to announce root cause of FAA router outage causing nationwide ground stop.
author: Ars Technica

title: California AG Rob Bonta subpoenas Nvidia over concerns about Huang’s China ties
content: California Attorney General Rob Bonta has issued a subpoena to Nvidia, citing concerns about Jensen Huang’s connections to China. Bonta said the company’s conduct and that of its former chief executive raise “bright red flags,” including possible misleading of investors.
summary: California Attorney General Rob Bonta issued a subpoena to Nvidia. He said the company’s conduct and its former CEO raise red flags, including concerns about Huang’s ties with China and possible investor misleadings.
author: TechCrunch

title: AI imposes hidden cognitive tax on lowest-paid workers
content:
AI is increasingly adding to the cognitive load of workers who are already stretched thin by unpredictable pay, insecure housing and mounting debt, with the lowest‑paid feeling the impact most acutely. The article argues that as the economy is reshaped by artificial intelligence, there is a growing need to rethink welfare systems to support these vulnerable workers.

The piece notes that throughout the history of economics, the human brain—responsible for directing labour, judgment and resilience—has rarely been considered an asset in its own right. The emerging AI economy is changing that perspective. As machines take on routine tasks, the value of human judgment, creativity and insights—qualities that only people can provide—has risen. Economists have coined the term “brain capital” to describe this shift.

Professor Dame Henrietta Moore, founder and director of the UCL Institute for Global Prosperity and co‑leader of The New Alignment, the institute’s G20 policy programme, is cited as a key figure in this discussion. Her work highlights the importance of recognising and supporting the cognitive contributions of workers in an AI‑driven economy.
summary: AI adds cognitive load to workers already stretched thin by unpredictable pay, insecure housing, and mounting debt, affecting lowest-paid workers the most. The emerging AI economy values judgment, creativity, and insights, leading economists to refer to this as brain capital.
author: Guardian Technology

title: Tech expert mum tests 17 baby monitors for picture quality, battery life
content:
A tech‑savvy new mother evaluated 17 baby monitors, assessing picture quality, battery life and reliability, and shared the models she recommends. She began using a video monitor after moving her infant into a separate bedroom, noting that the device allowed her to check on her child from a distance while the baby slept.

The review notes that baby monitors vary from basic audio‑only units to advanced video systems, some of which incorporate wearables or sensors to track breathing and heart rate, and others that use AI to analyse sleep patterns. All monitors consist of a baby unit placed near the child and a parent unit for listening or viewing; in video models the baby unit functions as a camera and the parent unit provides a screen. Many models are Wi‑Fi enabled, allowing live feeds to be accessed through a smartphone app, and the article includes security advice for such connections.
summary: She, a tech expert and new mother, tested 17 baby monitors evaluating picture quality, battery life and reliability. The monitors varied from simple audio units to video models with Wi‑Fi, wearables and AI sleep‑analysis features.
author: Guardian Technology

title: Outages hit Microsoft, United Airlines, JPMorgan Chase, US flights and NSA network
content:
Frontier AI models are said to be able to exploit software flaws more quickly than the world can respond, raising concerns that the risks extend beyond the cyber realm. The author notes that many people feel the world is “coming apart at the seams.”

Within the last week, outages crippled core services at Microsoft, United Airlines and JPMorgan Chase. Friday saw all U.S. domestic departures grounded for the second time since 9/11, and on Tuesday CNN reported that the NSA’s highly classified internal communications network went down. In each incident, the officials or companies involved stated that there was no evidence of a cyber‑attack.
summary: Frontier models can exploit software flaws faster than they can be fixed, creating risks beyond the cyber realm. Recent outages disrupted core services at Microsoft, United Airlines and JPMorgan Chase, grounded all US domestic departures, and took down the NSA’s internal communications network, with officials saying there was no evidence of a cyber‑attack.
author: Guardian Technology

title: Peter Gabriel shows keyboard duet with bonobo Kanzi and talks new album
content: From sampling to streaming, the rock legend has always been in thrall to technology – but is superintelligence a step too far? Back with an epic new album, he unpacks his remarkable ideas Peter Gabriel asks me to fetch my laptop: he wants to show me a video of himself playing a keyboard duet with a bonobo called Kanzi. In fairness, said footage is, as Gabriel suggests, “extraordinary”. Working with primatologist Sue Savage-Rumbaugh, who developed a means of communicating with bonobos involving sign language and a speech-synthesis keyboard, Gabriel plays droning chords on a synthesiser while Kanzi picks out complementary notes on a piano. “Look, she likes that note, which is a ninth, and then she finds the octave,” he enthuses as the video plays. “There’s a real musicality there.” It is all deeply unlikely, but it seems the perfect illustration of how easily a conversation with Gabriel can go wildly – if fascinatingly – off-piste. I’ve only been in his company for 10 minutes, long enough to ask a solitary question about his epic new album o\i: its 13 tracks last nearly 90 minutes, the result, he suggests, of a longstanding interest in African music “which made me realise that a song could last as long as a song could last”, and of “being old enough to think ‘fuck it’, really”. For anyone who feels that an hour and a half of exquisitely arranged, beautifully produced, occasionally deeply strange art rock – its sound shapeshifting from the folk-flecked A Hard Lesson to the glowing pop hues of Till Your Mind Is Shining – is too meagre an offering, it arrives in two versions: a “dark” mix by US producer Tchad Blake and a “bright” version that’s the handiwork of Mike “Spike” Stent, famed for working with everyone from U2 and Madonna to Frank Ocean and Harry Styles.
summary: Peter Gabriel shows a video of himself playing a keyboard duet with bonobo Kanzi, created with primatologist Sue Savage‑Rumbaugh. He says his new 13‑track, nearly 90‑minute album is available in a “dark” mix by Tchad Blake and a “bright” mix by Mike “Spike” Stent.
author: Guardian Technology

title: Vatican Museums showcase century of Popemobiles in new exhibition
content: The Vatican Museums are hosting an exhibition that traces a century of papal vehicles. Featuring eight historic cars—from Pope Pius XI’s Mercedes to Pope John Paul II’s Popemobile—the display shows how the Popes’ transportation has evolved, highlighting shifts in technology, curiosities and safety.
summary: The Vatican Museums are presenting an exhibition of eight historic papal cars, from Pius XI’s Mercedes to John Paul II’s Popemobile. The show traces a century of papal vehicle evolution, emphasizing technology, curiosities and safety.
author: Euronews

title: Vatican lifts 25‑metre Christmas tree in St Peter’s Square
content: A 25‑metre silver fir, described as a giant Christmas tree, was lifted into St Peter’s Square beside St Peter’s Basilica in Vatican City on Friday, 20 November 2026, marking the start of the season’s preparations. The tree, donated by a community in southern Italy, is scheduled to be unveiled on 7 December.
summary: A 25‑metre silver fir Christmas tree was lifted into St Peter’s Square in Vatican City on Friday 20 November 2026. The tree, donated by a community in southern Italy, will be unveiled on 7 December.
author: Euronews

title: UK anthem plays at EU summit as Prime Minister Andy Burnham meets EU leaders
content: UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham was welcomed by EU leaders in Brussels for a summit intended to strengthen post‑Brexit relations. At the meeting, the British anthem “God Save the King” was played, marking its first appearance at a UK–EU summit since Brexit.
summary: UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham was welcomed by EU leaders in Brussels for a summit aimed at strengthening post‑Brexit relations. God Save the King rang out for the first time since Brexit at the UK‑EU summit.
author: Euronews

title: Estonia to close five border checkpoints with Russia from Dec. 1 after GRU‑linked arson
content: Estonia will close its five border checkpoints with Russia on 1 December, with a review slated for six months later, after an attempted arson at a defence facility near Tallinn that Estonian authorities attribute to orders from Russian military intelligence. Rail services across the border will continue to operate.
summary: Estonia will close its five border checkpoints with Russia on 1 December, with a possible review after six months. The decision follows an attempted arson at a defence facility near Tallinn that authorities say was ordered by Russian military intelligence, while rail services will remain unaffected.
author: Euronews

title: NYC mayor proposes extending Rikers Island jail closure to 2032
content: New York City Mayor announced a plan to close the Rikers Island jail by 2032. The facility had previously been scheduled to shut down by August 2027 under City Council legislation passed in 2019. Extending the closure date to 2032 will require amending that law.
summary: The New York City mayor announced a plan to close the Rikers Island jail by 2032. The new deadline extends the original August 2027 target set by 2019 City Council legislation and will require a change to that law.
author: Euronews

title: Eight killed as Russian overnight strike damages Kyiv buildings, rescue teams search wreckage
content: A Russian overnight attack on Kyiv on Friday, 20 November 2026, killed eight people and damaged buildings and warehouses across the capital, according to the Associated Press. Firefighters fought blazes while emergency crews searched the wreckage, and police gathered evidence at the scene.
summary: A Russian overnight attack on Kyiv on Friday 20 November 2026 killed eight people and damaged buildings and warehouses across the capital. Firefighters fought blazes while emergency crews searched the wreckage and police collected evidence.
author: Euronews

title: UAE diplomat Lana Nusseibeh pledges relentless diplomacy in UN leadership bid
content: Emirati diplomat Lana Nusseibeh, a candidate to succeed António Guterres, told Euronews that the United Nations should refocus on its core purpose of peace, development and prosperity. She pledged “relentless diplomacy,” a leaner UN evaluated by results, and early action on conflicts such as the wars in Ukraine and Gaza if she is chosen.
summary: Lana Nusseibeh, an Emirati diplomat, is running to succeed António Guterres. She said the UN must return to its core purpose of peace, development and prosperity and pledged relentless diplomacy, a leaner UN judged on results, and early action on wars from Ukraine to Gaza if chosen.
author: Euronews

title: COP31 in Turkey stalls as draft deal omits fossil fuels
content:
UN climate negotiations at COP31 in Turkey are set to extend beyond the scheduled deadline on Friday as delegations remain deadlocked over a draft agreement that does not reference fossil fuels.  The stalemate is compounded by additional disputes that are slowing progress on the final text.

The talks unfold against a backdrop of heightened climate urgency, highlighted by heatwaves across Europe, severe flooding in Nepal and a record‑breaking El Niño that is boosting global temperatures.  France 24’s Environment Editor Valerie Dekimpe provides further coverage.
summary: The UN's COP31 climate talks in Turkey were set to run overtime on Friday as countries remained deadlocked over a draft deal that makes no mention of fossil fuels. The negotiations occur amid heatwaves in Europe, floods in Nepal and a record‑breaking El Niño that heighten urgency.
author: France 24

title: Burnham and von der Leyen call EU‑UK summit deal a turning point
content: British Prime Minister Andy Burnham described a “landmark” deal reached on Friday with the European Union, where the parties signed pacts on food exports, emissions‑trading schemes and youth mobility during a summit in Brussels. EU chief Ursula von der Leyen called the agreement a “turning point” in Britain‑EU ties following Brexit.
summary: British Prime Minister Andy Burnham said the Brussels summit pact on food exports, emissions‑trading schemes and youth mobility was a "landmark" deal. EU chief Ursula von der Leyen called the agreement a "turning point" in ties with Britain after Brexit.
author: France 24

title: Cincinnati Zoo's Fiona the hippo dies after swallowing a visitor's hat
content:
Cincinnati Zoo announced that Fiona, the 9‑year‑old hippo who became a worldwide sensation after her premature birth and early survival struggle nearly ten years ago, died on Thursday. Zoo officials said the animal swallowed a knit hat that had been accidentally thrown into her enclosure, leading to a medical emergency.

The zoo’s statement expressed “extreme sadness” and noted that veterinarians and keepers made multiple attempts to treat Fiona, but she did not survive the complications from the incident.
summary: Fiona, the Cincinnati Zoo hippo who became a global sensation, died Thursday at age nine from complications after swallowing a knit hat that was accidentally flung into her enclosure. Zoo officials said veterinarians and keepers made multiple attempts to treat her but she did not survive.
author: France 24

title: Less than 1% of Jamaica's coastline remains free for locals
content: Jamaica’s iconic white‑sandy shores are becoming less accessible to its residents. According to recent reporting, fewer than one percent of the island’s coastline remains freely open to locals, while the majority has been privatized for large hotel projects and private residences.
summary: Most of Jamaica's beaches are now off limits to local people. Less than 1% of the coastline is freely accessible, while the remainder has been privatized mainly for large hotel developments and private homes.
author: France 24

title: Spain to hold parliamentary election on Nov. 29 that could end Sanchez’s third term
content:
Spaniards are set to vote in a parliamentary election on November 29, a contest that could end the Socialist-led government and potentially result in a coalition between the right and the far right. This vote in one of the EU’s biggest and most influential member states carries significant implications for Europe. The election may also mark the end of Pedro Sanchez’s third term in office.

The prime minister faces political pressure stemming from two shocking train crashes and the migrant crisis in Spain’s North African exclave of Ceuta. These issues are central to the high stakes of the upcoming vote, which could reshape the political landscape in the region.
summary: Spain will hold a parliamentary election on November 29 that could end the Socialist‑led government and Pedro Sanchez’s third term. The prime minister may face political fallout from two train crashes and the migrant crisis in Ceuta, and a coalition between the right and the far right is possible.
author: France 24

title: Xi Jinping's Shenzhen trilateral with US president and Putin called diplomatic theatre
content:
Xi Jinping met with the U.S. president and Russia’s Vladimir Putin for trilateral talks in Shenzhen this week, presenting himself as a great statesman on the world stage.  

According to Seong‑Hyon Lee, an associate at Harvard University’s Asia Center, the Shenzhen trilateral has delivered few concrete outcomes, falling short on substantive deliverables.
summary: Xi Jinping met with the US president and Russia's Vladimir Putin for trilateral talks in Shenzhen this week. Seong-Hyon Lee, an associate at Harvard University Asia Center, says the trilateral has come up short on deliverables.
author: France 24

title: Dominique de Villepin announces presidential run in France
content: France’s former prime minister and foreign minister Dominique de Villepin announced on Friday that he is entering the presidential race. Villepin, noted internationally for his 2003 criticism of U.S. plans to invade Iraq, joins a crowded field of candidates seeking to succeed President Emmanuel Macron. Current polls suggest the contest could culminate in a run‑off between far‑right National Rally leader Marine Le Pen and hard‑left France Unbowed veteran Jean‑Luc Mélanchon.
summary: Former prime minister and foreign minister Dominique de Villepin said on Friday he is running for president. He enters a crowded field in which polls point to a possible run‑off between frontrunner Marine Le Pen of the far‑right National Rally (RN) and hard‑left France Unbowed (LFI) veteran Jean‑Luc Melenchon.
author: France 24

title: Uganda minister at COP31: 'We need a just transition'
content: Funding from wealthy countries to help deal with the impacts of climate change hasn't materialized, says Uganda's environment minister. The East African country is hoping oil and carbon credits will help boost finances.
summary: Funding from wealthy countries to help deal with the impacts of climate change hasn't materialized, says Uganda's environment minister. The East African country is hoping oil and carbon credits will help boost finances.
author: DW World

title: China’s Xi says Australia relationship has turned around after APEC talks
content: The leaders of Australia and China have held talks on sidelines of APEC summit. Australian PM Anthony Albanese is also slated to meet Chinese Premier Li Qiang.
summary: Chinese President Xi Jinping praised a turnaround in the relationship with Australia. Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese and Chinese Premier Li Qiang held talks on the sidelines of the APEC summit.
author: DW World

title: ICJ holds Myanmar responsible for Rohingya genocide, orders restitution
content: The International Court of Justice ruled that Myanmar bears responsibility for genocide against the Rohingya and ordered the country to provide restitution and reparations. Rohingya community members welcomed the decision but warned that securing genuine change will be a prolonged and difficult effort.
summary: The ICJ held Myanmar responsible for genocide against the Rohingya and ordered restitution and reparations. Community members hailed the ruling but cautioned that achieving real change will be long and hard.
author: DW World

title: Africa at COP31 in Antalya faces question of climate funding delivery
content: COP31 is concluding in Antalya, and African nations are focusing on whether the climate promises made at the summit will be converted into funding for communities that need support to cope with a warming world. The central question highlighted is the translation of pledges into tangible financial resources for Africa.
summary: COP31 is drawing to a close in Antalya. African countries are questioning whether climate promises will translate into funding for their communities to cope with a warming world.
author: DW World

title: Turkey takes control of pro-opposition broadcaster Sozcu TV
content: Turkey has placed the pro‑opposition broadcaster Sozcu TV under state control. The move follows a series of raids and arrests targeting media outlets and marks the third major broadcaster taken over by the government in the past year.
summary: Turkey has taken control of the opposition broadcaster Sozcu TV. It is the third major pro‑opposition Turkish broadcaster placed under state control in a year amid raids and arrests.
author: DW World

title: EU and UK agree landmark youth mobility and trade deals to rebuild ties
content: The European Union and the United Kingdom have reached “landmark” agreements covering youth mobility and trade. Leaders from both sides praised the deals as they work to rebuild ties after Brexit.
summary: The European Union and the United Kingdom have agreed on landmark deals on youth mobility and trade. Leaders on both sides praised the agreements as they seek to rebuild ties.
author: DW World

title: Afghan Taliban accuse Pakistan of aiding anti‑Taliban resistance groups
content: The Taliban government in Afghanistan has accused Pakistan of providing aid and shelter to armed resistance groups operating against it. The allegations arise amid heightened tensions between the two countries and are expected to further deepen the diplomatic rift separating Afghanistan and Pakistan.
summary: The Taliban rulers in Afghanistan have accused Pakistan of aiding and sheltering armed resistance groups. The allegations come amid heightened tensions and could deepen the rift between the two neighbors.
author: DW World

title: UN officials say AI gives predators new ways to target children
content: Senior United Nations officials warned on Thursday that artificial intelligence is providing predators and criminal groups with new methods to groom, extort and exploit children. They said protective measures are lagging behind the rapid development of AI‑enabled tactics.
summary: AI is providing predators and criminal groups with new methods to groom, extort and exploit children. Senior UN officials warned on Thursday that protection efforts are not keeping pace.
author: UN News

title: UN scales up accountability for peacekeeper paternity claims as 500 cases unresolved
content: The United Nations said it will introduce new accountability measures aimed at better supporting children fathered by peacekeepers, noting that 500 paternity and child‑support claims remain unresolved. The announcement was made on Thursday by Catherine Pollard, the UN Under‑Secretary‑General for Management Strategy, Policy and Compliance.
summary: The UN is adding new accountability measures to better support children fathered by peacekeepers, as 500 paternity and child support claims remain unresolved. The announcement was made by Under-Secretary-General for Management Strategy, Policy and Compliance Catherine Pollard on Thursday.
author: UN News

title: Battle over GPS and radio signals threatens civilian safety
content: Safe journeys for aid convoys, passenger jets and cargo ships rely on GPS, satellite navigation and traditional radio transmissions. According to the report, these signals are increasingly being blocked or faked, a development that is raising civilian safety concerns.
summary: Safe journeys for aid convoys, passenger jets and cargo ships depend on GPS, satellite navigation and radio transmissions. Those signals are increasingly being blocked or faked, raising civilian safety concerns.
author: UN News

content: Aid and development agencies in Afghanistan warned on Friday that an escalating “assault” on the rights and freedoms of women and girls is hindering an increasing number of them from obtaining vital medical care, including pregnant women seeking help. The agencies said the restrictions are preventing access to necessary health services.

title: Youth protests in 20+ European nations over cost of living, education, military spending
content: Activists in more than 20 countries demonstrate over cost of living, learning conditions and rising military spending Students and young workers have taken to the streets in more than 20 European countries in coordinated protests over the surging cost of living and housing, deteriorating learning conditions and rising military spending. Activists from more than 50 groups in countries including Belgium, France, Germany, Greece, Italy, Portugal, Spain and the UK held rallies on Friday, lighting flares, burning cardboard models of tanks and waving placards, many reading “fight for our future”.

title: EU says it wants closest possible relationship with UK after Brexit reset deal
content:
The President of the European Council stated that the EU “remains open to have the closest possible relationship” with the United Kingdom following the agreement of a Brexit “reset” deal. According to a senior correspondent, the deal is now tied to a separate agreement on tuition fees for EU citizens, a move described by EU sources as intended to neutralise the leverage the UK could gain over the next six months.

Senior diplomats confirmed that the EU will defer the tuition‑fees component for an additional six months. The deferral is presented as a way to give the UK bargaining power in parallel talks about including the United Kingdom in the “Made in Europe” legislation aimed at protecting EU supply chains from China. At the same time, linking the food‑and‑drink agreement to the tuition‑fees issue is portrayed as a strategy to curb any current UK leverage.

French officials have reiterated that the UK will not receive voting rights on legislation concerning food and drink. During a meeting with businesses in Brussels, Prime Minister Burnham said the EU deal would contribute up to 0.5 percent to the UK’s GDP, describing the arrangement as “pretty much there” and “a really good deal.” Treasury analysis released the same day echoed the 0.5 percent GDP impact, calling it the “single biggest growth intervention in this Parliament.”
summary: EU says it wants closest possible relationship with UK after Brexit reset deal.

title: NSW health warns vapes after three users hospitalized with etomidate exposure
content:
Three people in New South Wales lost consciousness and were hospitalised after using certain vape products. Tests on the vape liquids used by the patients confirmed the presence of etomidate, an unregulated anaesthetic agent.  

NSW Health issued a public warning on Friday about vape liquids containing etomidate. The warning notes that etomidate is a strong, fast‑acting sedative used as a general anaesthetic overseas, but it is not registered for medical use in Australia.
summary: Three people who used certain vape liquids in New South Wales lost consciousness and were hospitalized, and testing showed they had the unregulated anaesthetic agent etomidate in their system. NSW health issued a public warning about vape liquids containing etomidate, which is not registered for medical use in Australia.

content:

title: Cuban asylum seeker Luis Cora Pérez ends ICE hunger strike after painful force-feeding
content:
Luis Alejandro Cora Pérez, a 32‑year‑old Cuban asylum seeker, sent text messages to the Guardian from inside an ICE detention center in Texas. In the messages he described the conditions of his three‑month hunger strike, saying he remained weak and dizzy. He noted that after five days of eating regular food, the staff would place a feeding tube in him if he refused to eat.

Cora Pérez explained that the pain of the force‑feeding was too great, and that this discomfort ultimately led him to end his hunger strike.
summary: Luis Alejandro Cora Pérez, a 32‑year‑old Cuban asylum seeker detained by ICE in Texas, said he was still weak and dizzy after three months without eating. He told the Guardian he ended his hunger strike because the pain of being force‑fed through a tube was unbearable.

title: California coastal towns face biggest waves in decades as 30‑ft swells hit
content:
Multiple coastal hazard warnings were issued this week across California after successive low‑pressure areas generated powerful swells and large breaking waves. Beaches and piers were closed last weekend as waves crashed into the coastline, and offshore National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration buoys recorded wave heights of more than 30 ft (9 m) on Friday. The Monterey buoy logged a height of 34.1 ft, the highest reading in 30 years.

The warnings extend from last weekend through Friday night, with forecasts of 10‑18 ft waves and local sets of 18‑22 ft for San Luis Obispo County beaches and Santa Barbara County central‑coast beaches. The same Pacific storm systems are bringing unsettled conditions across the western United States, including heavy rain, mountain snow and strong winds. Record‑breaking rainfall affected San Francisco on Wednesday, and heavy rain caused a power loss for 32,000 customers in Sacramento. A further low‑pressure area is expected to bring significant moisture to southern Oregon and northern California, with more than 100 mm (4 in) of rain forecast by Sunday night and additional snowfall anticipated for areas such as Donner Pass in the northern Sierra Nevada.
summary: California coastal towns face biggest waves in decades as 30‑ft swells hit.

title: Nonprofit Common Space to launch humanitarian satellite with Satellogic in July 2027
content:
Nonprofit Common Space has announced that its first “humanitarian satellite” will launch in 2027, marking the beginning of a six‑satellite constellation aimed at providing high‑resolution Earth‑observing imagery for first responders, journalists, scientists and human‑rights investigators. The organization plans to operate on a “club‑good model,” sharing infrastructure and costs across a broad community to enable low‑cost, high‑quality access to imagery that is currently largely proprietary or expensive.

The first satellite in the constellation will be built by Satellogic, an Argentine‑U.S. geospatial intelligence company. Common Space selected Satellogic’s NewSat Mark V after a competitive request‑for‑proposal process. The microsatellite, 32 inches (82 cm) long and 85 pounds (38.5 kg) on Earth, will resolve ground features as small as 27.5 inches (70 cm) from low Earth orbit, with proprietary algorithms boosting the resolution to 19.7 inches (50 cm). Satellogic will handle launch preparations and satellite operations, which are expected to last at least five years in orbit.

The satellite is scheduled to launch in July 2027 on a rocket that has not yet been announced. Satellogic will manage the mission, drawing on its experience of flying 61 Earth‑observing satellites to date, all of which deployed successfully. The company’s vice president of space systems, Luciano Giesso, emphasized that the partnership aligns with Common Space’s philosophy of democratizing persistent global intelligence for humanitarian responders and journalists.

Common Space is currently raising funds to expand the constellation to six satellites, with a goal of having all six in place by 2030. The expanded network would provide daily high‑resolution coverage of priority areas, according to the nonprofit. The launch of the first satellite represents a concrete step toward the organization’s vision of making high‑resolution Earth imagery widely available for public‑interest purposes.
summary: The first satellite in a constellation designed for humanitarian use will lift off next year, if all goes according to plan. The nonprofit Common Space plans to assemble a six-spacecraft constellation of Earth-observing satellites, whose high-resolution imagery will aid first responders, journalists, scientists and human-rights investigators around the world.

title: The Altruists: Julia Garner and Anthony Boyle star in FTX fraud drama
content: Julia Garner and Anthony Boyle play the FTX founders behind ‘the greatest fraud ever committed’ in the US. It’s a mind-boggling story – just make sure you don’t miss a single moment What happens when you put really stupid clever people in charge of the world? Not as presidents (they currently trend mostly towards the merely stupid) or prime ministers (generally neither really stupid nor really clever), but in charge of the real world, which is to say the online world, the one that really governs us? We are watching that play out day by day, but if you have enough slack left in your dread-system, a cortisol spike yet to execute, why not add a warning from history to your consumption of horrors? Welcome to The Altruists, a breakneck breakdown of the brief career of Sam Bankman-Fried (played by Anthony Boyle) who, with his on-off girlfriend Caroline Ellison (played by Julia Garner), set up the cryptocurrency exchange FTX with the belief that it would revolutionise finance and – as the increasingly absurd/dishonest/knowingly satirical Silicon Valley mantra has it – make the world a better place. A very few years later, FTX – worth $36bn (£27bn) at its peak – collapsed and in 2023 the pair were convicted of various charges deriving from what the trial judge called “the greatest financial fraud ever perpetrated in this country”. Ellison was sentenced to two years in prison after testifying against Bankman-Fried. Bankman-Fried is serving 25 years and was ordered to forfeit $11bn (£8.3bn). He says he is innocent and is applying to the supreme court to review his conviction.
summary: The series depicts the rise and collapse of cryptocurrency exchange FTX, focusing on founders Sam Bankman-Fried and Caroline Ellison. Bankman-Fried is serving a 25-year sentence and has forfeited $11 billion, while Ellison received a two-year prison term after testifying against him.
author: Guardian Culture

title: ‘Sam-Bankman Fried messaged me from prison’: rising star Anthony Boyle on playing the disgraced tech bro – and a zero-hours bike courier
content: The actor’s latest roles see him go from a delivery guy on £40 a day to the notorious crypto scammer who stole more than $10bn. His sympathies are clear: ‘I wasn’t brought up to care about money,’ he says In the spring of 2019, Anthony Boyle went to see Cillian Murphy in Grief Is the Thing with Feathers at St Ann’s Warehouse in Brooklyn. Afterwards, the 24-year-old actor hung around the stage door. “There were 500 people queueing up for Cillian, but I was the only one who wanted to meet Enda Walsh,” says Boyle, laughing. When the Dublin-born writer Walsh finally appeared, Boyle introduced himself. He was from west Belfast, he’d read Walsh’s plays at drama school, and it was his dream to work with him one day. He asked if Walsh would like to come and see him on Broadway, where he was playing Scorpius Malfoy, son of Draco, in Harry Potter and the Cursed Child. How did he respond? Boyle grins. “He was sort of like: ‘Oh.’” Since Walsh never went to see The Cursed Child, Boyle assumed the writer had immediately forgotten about him. Then, a few years later, he received a letter from Walsh explaining that he was adapting Keiran Goddard’s 2024 novel I See Buildings Fall Like Lightning, about five close friends from a council estate in Birmingham who find themselves questioning everything about their precarious lives as they hit 30. He had scripted the part of Patrick, a politically outspoken graduate working as a zero-hours bike courier to support his young family, with Boyle in mind. Clio Barnard was on board to direct.
summary: ‘Sam-Bankman Fried messaged me from prison’: rising star Anthony Boyle on playing the disgraced tech bro – and a zero-hours bike courier.

title: Jeff Buckley was a 90s indie darling. Now gen Z think he’s the ‘yearner final boss’
content: With his unguarded lyricism and earnest delivery, the late singer-songwriter is having a moment among a generation that fetishizes unrequited desire Sydney Tripoli has collected Jeff Buckley memorabilia since 2019. She keeps her collection of T-shirts, posters, vinyl and other merch celebrating the late singer-songwriter in what she affectionately calls her “Buckley box”. content:

The purchase is reportedly being made by San Diego Padres owners José E Feliciano and his wife, Kwanza Jones. This transaction would set a new record for a WNBA team, surpassing the previous high of $300 million paid for the Connecticut Sun in March.

content:

According to social media announcements released Wednesday night, Taylor was warming up on May 26 when he was accidentally struck on the head and collapsed on the field. He was subsequently airlifted to a local hospital, where he was placed on a ventilator in critical condition.

During his prolonged hospitalization, Major League Baseball players showed support for Taylor. The incident occurred in May, and the boy remained in the hospital until his death.
summary: Xavier Taylor, a 12-year-old New Jersey boy, died after being struck on the head during a Little League game on May 26. He had been hospitalized in critical condition on a ventilator since the incident.

title: World marathon champion Peres Jepchirchir banned for three years over doping
content:
Reigning women’s world marathon champion Peres Jepchirchir has received a three-year ban for EPO use. The 33-year-old athlete, who secured Olympic gold in Tokyo in 2021 and world gold in 2025, had her initial sanction reduced by one year because she chose not to challenge the results of a blood test taken before winning the Sydney Marathon in August.

This decision marks a difficult period for Kenyan distance running, as two other leading athletes from the country were also punished for doping violations.

title: Houston Texans defeat Indianapolis Colts 26-3 in Thursday night win
content:
The Houston Texans defeated the Indianapolis Colts 26-3 on Thursday night, securing their first home victory of the season and keeping their playoff hopes alive. Quarterback CJ Stroud led the offense with 194 passing yards and three touchdowns, exploiting a Colts secondary missing injured starting cornerbacks Sauce Gardner and Charvarius Ward. This win allowed the Texans to bounce back from a 27-24 loss to Cleveland the previous weekend.

The Texans relied on a strong defensive performance to dominate the hapless Colts, who have a 3-26 record. Stroud’s accuracy against the weakened defensive backfield was a key factor in the lopsided result, marking a significant improvement for Houston after their recent setback against Cleveland.
summary: CJ Stroud threw for 194 yards and three touchdowns as the Houston Texans defeated the Indianapolis Colts 26-3. The win marked Houston's first victory at home this season and allowed them to keep their playoff hopes alive.

title: Sandpapergate evolves from ball‑tampering scandal to ongoing outrage, says Jonathan Horn
content: Nothing about the responses and reprisals to Australia’s ball tampering have been proportional in a story where the truth probably lies somewhere in the middle Who said long-form journalism is dead? As Matt Renshaw nudged his ones and twos in an already forgotten ODI match, the broadcasters were scanning Cameron Bancroft’s 4000-word essay. SEN’s Gerard Whateley was calling for a comprehensive judicial inquiry, “a little bit like a coroner’s inquest,” with witnesses compelled to attend and be subjected to cross examination. Cricket Australia’s “forum”, announced a few hours earlier, had already been skittled. Nothing in the eight years since a piece of sandpaper was taken on to the field in Cape Town, including the publication of Usman Khawaja’s book Sabr, had been as revelatory as Bancroft’s first-person account. But as always with this story, we were bracing for the next press conference, the next podcast, the next corroborating statement, the next counterclaim, the next overreaction.
summary: Nothing about the responses and reprisals to Australia’s ball tampering have been proportional in a story where the truth probably lies somewhere in the middle Who said long-form journalism is dead? content: Multi-million dollar sale comes despite a federal judge in Hawaii voiding the environmental clearance it had been given to proceed The US has carried out its first ever deep-sea mining lease sales off the coast of American Samoa, despite an adverse court ruling earlier this week and mounting local opposition. title: Singapore reports 65% decline in cervical cancer mortality since 1990
content:
Cervical cancer mortality in Singapore has declined by 65% since 1990, though screening gaps persist. The condition remains one of the few cancers potentially eliminable through human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccination, regular screening, and timely treatment of precancerous changes. Despite these effective prevention and treatment measures, global cervical cancer deaths are projected to increase by nearly 40% by 2050.

These findings come from a study involving researchers from the Yong Loo Lin School of Medicine, National University of Singapore (NUS Medicine), and the Institute for Health Metrics and Evaluation (IHME) at the University of Washington. The research highlights the contrast between Singapore’s significant progress and the anticipated rise in global mortality rates.
summary: Singapore has seen a 65% decline in cervical cancer mortality since 1990, yet screening gaps remain. A study by researchers from the Yong Loo Lin School of Medicine, NUS Medicine, and the Institute for Health Metrics and Evaluation projected that global cervical cancer deaths will rise by nearly 40% by 2050.

title: New Ophiopogon longiscapus Species Discovered in Yunnan Wenshan Reserve
content: Botanists have described a new mondo grass species, Ophiopogon longiscapus, from the Yunnan Wenshan National Nature Reserve in southeastern China. The plant is named for its unusually long flowering stalk, or scape.
summary: Botanists described a new Ophiopogon species in the Yunnan Wenshan National Nature Reserve, southeastern China. The species, named Ophiopogon longiscapus, was named for its unusually long flowering stalk, or scape.
author: Phys.org

title: Innovative technology offers a bold new vision for monitoring ocean health
content: MBARI's research vessel Paragon departed from Moss Landing early in October, carrying three robots on its deck. The launch occurred as Monterey Bay showcased its marine environment, underscoring the use of innovative technology for monitoring ocean health.
summary: Innovative technology offers a bold new vision for monitoring ocean health.
author: Phys.org

title: Researchers Build Structured-Light Systems in Three Dimensions
content:
Structured‑light technology has emerged as a vital tool in modern optics, enabling researchers to shape light fields by controlling amplitude, phase, polarization, and spatial mode. These engineered fields extend beyond the capabilities of conventional laser beams and are being applied in communications, imaging, sensing, optical computing, and quantum photonics.

Despite these advances, many structured‑light systems still depend on multiple discrete optical components. The components require careful alignment and occupy significant space, limiting compactness and ease of use in practical applications.
summary: Structured light allows shaping amplitude, phase, polarization and spatial mode to create light fields beyond conventional laser beams. Many current structured-light systems still rely on multiple discrete optical components that require careful alignment and occupy significant space.
author: Phys.org

title: AI virtual cell technology may reveal how genetic changes and drugs alter cells
content: Artificial intelligence models today can predict whether a person carrying a genetic change will develop a disease. However, they fall short of answering two critical questions: why the disease occurs and how to design an effective treatment. AI virtual‑cell technology is being explored as a way to reveal how genetic alterations and drugs alter cellular behavior.
summary: Current artificial intelligence models can predict whether a person with a genetic change will develop a disease. However, they cannot explain why the disease occurs or how to design a treatment.
author: Phys.org

title: IEA report says extreme weather raises risks to global oil and gas shipping
content: The International Energy Agency reports that extreme weather events are increasingly threatening international oil and natural gas shipping. According to the new IEA report, such events could damage critical infrastructure, disrupt major trade routes and jeopardize energy security.
summary: A new IEA report says extreme weather events are creating significant risks for international oil and natural gas shipping. The report warns that such events could damage critical infrastructure, disrupt major trade routes and threaten energy security.
author: Phys.org

title: UCT research: Nature-based solutions must shift to power-sharing in informal settlements
content:
New research from UCT finds that nature‑based solutions for climate adaptation are failing informal settlements.  
The study argues that solutions must shift from mere participation to power‑sharing partnerships that acknowledge residents’ lived experiences and their relationships with nature.
summary: New research from UCT indicates that nature-based solutions for climate adaptation are failing informal settlements. The study argues these solutions must move beyond participation to power-sharing partnerships that recognize lived experiences and relationships with nature.
author: Phys.org

title: MIT study finds data centers harm air quality far from their locations
content: A new study by MIT researchers indicates that the rapid expansion of artificial intelligence data centers causes negative health and air quality impacts in regions far from the physical facilities.
summary: The rapid expansion of data centers for artificial intelligence causes negative health and air quality impacts in regions far from where the brick‑and‑mortar facilities are located. The findings are reported in a new study by MIT researchers.
author: Phys.org

title: Scientists link CDK12 gene mutation to aggressive prostate cancer
content: Scientists discovered a rare inherited mutation in the CDK12 gene linked to aggressive prostate cancer. All five identified carriers developed metastatic disease between ages 44 and 62. The finding could lead to expanded genetic testing, helping families uncover hidden cancer risks and potentially detect the disease while it is still treatable.
summary: Researchers identified a rare inherited mutation in the CDK12 gene associated with aggressive prostate cancer, noting that all five carriers developed metastatic disease between ages 44 and 62. This discovery may enable expanded genetic testing to help families uncover hidden cancer risks and detect the disease while it is still treatable.
author: Science Daily

title: Scientists Narrow Search for Stonehenge's Six-Ton Altar Stone, Point to Scotland
content:
A new investigation into Stonehenge’s six‑ton Altar Stone has yielded fresh clues while eliminating several earlier theories. Researchers have ruled out a Welsh origin and now consider the massive sandstone slab to have come from northeastern Scotland.

Despite this narrowed focus, scientists have yet to locate an exact source match for the stone, leaving the mystery of its provenance unresolved.
summary: Researchers have ruled out several suspected sources for Stonehenge’s six‑ton Altar Stone. The slab, once thought to be from Wales, is now believed to have come from northeastern Scotland, though no exact match has been found.
author: Science Daily

title: Excessive Exercise May Leave Brain in Overdrive
content:
Scientists discovered that mice subjected to prolonged, intense training without adequate recovery exhibited elevated dopamine levels in a brain region associated with memory and emotions. These elevated levels persisted for at least 48 hours after the exercise sessions ended.

This finding offers a potential explanation for why overtrained athletes may experience symptoms such as insomnia, anxiety, and persistent fatigue, although the study did not directly measure these specific conditions in the animals.
summary: Scientists found that mice subjected to prolonged, intense training had elevated dopamine levels in a brain region linked to memory and emotions, even 48 hours after exercising. The discovery could help explain why overtrained athletes sometimes struggle with insomnia, anxiety, and persistent fatigue, although these symptoms were not directly measured.
author: Science Daily

title: Study finds Antarctica's ice cliffs stabilize rather than collapse catastrophically
content: A new study indicates that Antarctica’s towering ice cliffs may be less prone to catastrophic collapse than previously thought. By tracking over 15,000 ice cliffs, researchers found that even the tallest formations, which can collapse at alarming speeds, often stabilize rather than triggering an unstoppable chain reaction. The study suggests that underwater ridges, surrounding water, and broken ice provide natural defenses against further collapse.
summary: A new study tracking more than 15,000 ice cliffs suggests they are less vulnerable to catastrophic collapse than previously feared. Researchers found that underwater ridges, surrounding water, and broken ice help stabilize the tallest cliffs.
author: Science Daily

title: BepiColombo Arrives at Mercury, Prepares for Second‑Ever Orbit
content:
The BepiColombo double probe has arrived at Mercury after a journey exceeding eight years and 6 billion miles. This joint European-Japanese mission is set to become the second in history to enter orbit around the smallest planet in the solar system. Flight controllers are scheduled to fire the spacecraft’s thrusters on Saturday to initiate the orbital insertion.

Once in orbit, the mission will map Mercury’s surface and study its interior. These activities aim to provide insights into the planet’s unusually large core, contributing to the exploration of this barely explored world.
summary: BepiColombo Arrives at Mercury, Prepares for Second‑Ever Orbit.
author: Guardian Science

title: Cyclone Xavier Becomes Record-Setting Category 5 Storm in Southwest Pacific
content:
On November 15, 2026, the Fiji Meteorological Service began issuing updates regarding a slow-moving tropical disturbance located northeast of Samoa and the Cook Islands. Within days, this system intensified rapidly into one of the most intense November tropical cyclones the region has seen in decades. Named Xavier, the storm developed in an environment characterized by minimal wind shear and sea surface temperatures of 29 degrees Celsius (84 degrees Fahrenheit), conditions well above the threshold required to sustain and strengthen developing tropical cyclones. Xavier was the second named storm of the 2026 season, following a short-lived October storm named Wati.

NASA satellite data indicated that Xavier churned along the southwestern edge of a massive tongue of warm water stretching from the west coast of South America to the central Pacific, a sign of the El Niño present in the region since June. When the Moderate Resolution Imaging Spectroradiometer on NASA’s Aqua satellite captured an image at 02:53 Universal Time on November 17, 2026, forecasters estimated Xavier had maximum winds of about 195 kilometers (120 miles) per hour. Later that day, winds reached a peak intensity of 220 kilometers (140 miles) per hour, classifying the storm as a Category 5 on the regional cyclone intensity scale or a Category 4 on the Saffir-Simpson scale. Colorado State University hurricane expert Phil Klotzbach noted that Xavier ranks as the strongest November tropical cyclone east of the international date line on record.

The storm’s formation east of the date line, near the northern Cook Islands, was unusual but aligns with research indicating that storm activity in the region typically shifts northeast during El Niño years. Studies also suggest that El Niño tends to fuel storms that strengthen at an unusually rapid pace. According to news reports, Xavier damaged homes and caused power disruptions as it passed the northern Cook Islands. The system subsequently encountered dry air and a less favorable wind shear environment, causing it to weaken as it pushed westward and reducing the threat to Samoa and American Samoa.

Looking ahead, the Fiji Meteorological Service projects that the region could see between 11 and 15 named tropical cyclones this season, with the greatest risk located east of the international date line. Storm activity in the Southwest Pacific basin typically peaks in February, suggesting Xavier may be one of several storms to affect the area in the coming months. The image accompanying this report was taken by Lauren Dauphin using MODIS data from NASA EOSDIS LANCE and GIBS/Worldview, with the story written by Adam Voiland.
summary: Cyclone Xavier intensified rapidly in the Southwest Pacific, reaching peak winds of 220 km/h (140 mph) and becoming the strongest November tropical cyclone east of the international date line on record. The storm damaged homes and caused power disruptions in the northern Cook Islands before weakening and reducing the threat to Samoa and American Samoa.
author: NASA News

title: Voyager 1 receives Morse code message from Earth, one light-day away
content: APOD Science APOD APOD: 2026 November… Today’s APOD Archive Submissions Index Search Calendar RSS Education About Discuss APOD Astronomy Picture of the Day Discover the cosmos! Each day a different image or photograph of our fascinating universe is featured, along with a brief explanation written by a professional astronomer. V-G-R Explanation: On November 17, fans of interstellar spaceflight around planet Earth were invited to shine a message into the night sky. Traced by a flashlight beam switched on and off, the dashes and dots of a Morse code message captured in this time exposure from the Emirates Astronomical Observatory, are read V-G-R. That’s a call sign for the Voyager 1 spacecraft currently in interstellar space some 26 billion kilometers away. How long did it take the message to reach humanity’s most distant interstellar spacecraft? Traveling at the speed of light, the answer is one day. In fact, the Voyager 1 spacecraft was confirmed to reach its one light-day distance milestone on November 18, at 10:16:07 UTC, nearly 50 years after launch in 1977. For extra credit, fans of math can calculate that at one light-day per 50 years, Voyager 1 will reach its one light-year (365 light-days) distance milestone in about 18,250 years. Tomorrow’s picture: pixels in space Date: November 20, 2026 Credit & Copyright: Apostolos Kyriazis Authors & editors: Jerry Bonnell, Cecilia Chirenti, Robert Nemiroff, Keighley Rockcliffe A service of: ASD at NASA / GSFC, NASA Science Activation & Michigan Tech. U. Random APOD Generator Yesterday’s Image APOD: 2026 November 19 – The Horsehead and Flame Nebulas Tomorrow’s Image
summary: On November 17, fans used a flashlight beam at the Emirates Astronomical Observatory to send a Morse code message to Voyager 1, which was captured in a time exposure. The message traveled at the speed of light and reached Voyager 1 one day later, on November 18 at 10:16:07 UTC, marking its one light-day milestone.
author: NASA News

title: Gig Work Invades Nursing Homes, Leading to Dangerous Mistakes
content: A WIRED and Proof News investigation has found that inspection reports of elder‑care facilities reveal a serious problem: when new workers receive little or no onboarding, dangerous mistakes can occur and nurses become overwhelmed. The reports highlight the risks of gig work in nursing homes.
summary: Inspection reports reveal that elder care facilities often lack proper worker onboarding. This can cause dangerous mistakes and overwhelm nurses, according to a WIRED and Proof News investigation.
author: Wired

title: FAA Ground Stop Causes Chaotic Hours as Aviation Communications System Instability Persists
content:
The FAA ground stop occurred when instability in the complex US aviation communications system caused chaotic hours for air traffic controllers and pilots.  

Nearly a week later, officials still do not fully know what happened.
summary: Instability in the US aviation communications system caused chaotic hours for air traffic controllers and pilots. Nearly a week later, officials still do not fully know what happened.
author: Wired

title: Cincinnati Zoo’s 9‑year‑old hippo Fiona dies after ingesting a knit hat
content: Fiona, the 9‑year‑old hippo at the Cincinnati Zoo who was celebrated for surviving a premature birth, has died after ingesting a knit hat. Veterinary experts note that even a 2,500‑pound animal can succumb to complications from consuming such an object.
summary: Fiona, a 9‑year‑old hippo at the Cincinnati Zoo, died after eating a knit hat. Veterinary experts said the 2,500‑pound animal could succumb to complications from the hat, noting she was known for surviving a premature birth.
author: Wired

title: Walgreens Photo Coupons Offer Up to 70% Off Premium Wall Decor and More This November 2026
content: Walgreens is offering coupons that can save up to 70 % on premium wall decor, stationery, and personalized gifts, as well as beauty, lenses, and health products during the fall season. Customers can apply a verified Walgreens coupon code to receive these discounts.
summary: A verified Walgreens coupon code provides discounts of up to 70% off premium wall decor, stationery, and personalized gifts. The coupons also apply to beauty, lenses, and health products during this fall.
author: Wired

title: Sonos Launches Black Friday Sale: Up to 30% Off Speakers and Soundbars
content:
Sonos has launched its Black Friday sale, offering discounts on a range of speakers and soundbars through November 30. The promotion includes price reductions from Sonos, Amazon, and Best Buy, with savings highlighted for each product.

The Arc Ultra soundbar is available for $849, a $250 discount from its original price. The model supports Dolby Atmos, adds Bluetooth connectivity, and features a Quick Tune function that uses built‑in microphones to adjust audio automatically for the room. It can be paired with a Sonos subwoofer such as the Sub 4, which is part of a bundle priced at $1,499, a $499 discount. The Arc Ultra’s price is listed at $1,099 at Sonos and Best Buy, and $849 at Amazon.

The second‑generation Sonos Beam has a new low price of $339, a $160 discount. It supports Dolby Atmos and HDMI eARC, and can fill a room with rich, clear audio. The Beam’s price is $499 at Sonos and Best Buy, and $339 at Amazon.

For those seeking a smart speaker, the Era 100 SL is offered at $149, a $40 discount. The SL model lacks a built‑in mic, so it does not support voice controls, but it delivers stereo sound with dual tweeters and a large woofer. The standard Era 100 is available for $179 at Amazon and Best Buy. Both models are priced at $189 at Sonos.

The portable Sonos Play is available for $239, a $60 discount. It offers up to 24 hours of battery life, an IP67 rating, and a removable carrying loop. The Play supports Wi‑Fi, Bluetooth, and can be grouped with other Sonos speakers over Bluetooth when Wi‑Fi is not available. Its price is $299 at Sonos and Best Buy, and $239 at Amazon.

Finally, the Sonos Ace headphones are discounted to $229, a $120 reduction. The headphones provide powerful, detailed sound, solid noise cancellation, and a transparency mode. They support up to 30 hours of playback on a single charge and include a TV Audio Swap feature that lets users transfer audio from a compatible Sonos soundbar. The Ace is priced at $399 at Sonos and Best Buy, and $229 at Amazon.
summary: Sonos is offering up to 30% off its speakers and soundbars during a Black Friday sale that runs through November 30th. The sale includes discounts on the Arc Ultra soundbar, Sonos Play portable speaker, and Sonos Era 100 SL smart speaker.
author: The Verge

title: Instagram‑Amazon Affiliate Integration Sparks Creator Skepticism
content:
Instagram announced a new integration with Amazon this month, allowing creators to link their accounts and automatically tag products with affiliate links. This feature enables influencers to earn commissions when followers purchase tagged items, with limits of up to 30 product links in a Reel or 20 in a feed post. The update aims to simplify a process that previously required influencers to use various workarounds to share affiliate links on social media.

Despite the convenience offered by the new tool, some content creators remain skeptical about the program. These individuals are questioning who ultimately benefits from the integration, expressing suspicion regarding the advantages of the new affiliate structure for influencers.
summary: Instagram announced a new integration with Amazon that lets creators link products to their affiliate accounts. Some influencers question who benefits, as the feature allows up to 30 product links in a Reel or 20 in a feed.
author: The Verge

title: US IT Outages: How to Tell Cyberattacks from Accidental Failures
content:
Over the past week, a series of high‑profile IT disruptions rattled U.S. infrastructure. A mass Microsoft Exchange outage shut down services for thousands of companies. A Federal Aviation Administration technical error grounded planes nationwide. Software problems at JPMorgan Chase triggered further disruption, while a United Airlines system glitch delayed flights again. An NSA classified network experienced downtime, leaving staff at Fort Meade waiting to return to their offices.

These incidents, occurring on four consecutive business days, coincided with a U.S. war with Iran and growing concerns about AI‑enabled hacking. Observers saw the sequence as more than mere coincidence, but no evidence has surfaced linking the failures to one another or to malicious actors.

Cybersecurity analysts, along with reporters at WIRED, are tasked with distinguishing accidental outages from potential cyberattacks. The article emphasizes that, despite the timing and context, the incidents remain unexplained and have not been proven to be the result of hacking.
summary: Over the past week, major IT services—including Microsoft Exchange, the FAA, JPMorgan Chase, United Airlines, and an NSA classified network—experienced outages. Analysts must determine whether these incidents were accidental or the result of cyberattacks.
author: Ars Technica

title: NASA's Artemis Shakeup Adds Burden to Orion Spacecraft
content:
NASA has announced a major revision to its Artemis program that will alter how astronauts reach the Moon. The changes are aimed at giving the agency’s lunar lander partners—SpaceX’s Starship and Blue Origin’s Blue Moon—greater flexibility in their lunar missions.

Under the new plan, Starship will dock with NASA’s Orion spacecraft while still in Earth orbit and then travel to the Moon together. For Blue Moon, the rendezvous with Orion will be moved from Earth orbit to low‑lunar orbit. These adjustments are designed to benefit the landers but place additional demands on Orion, which Lockheed Martin builds for NASA.

To explain the implications for the Orion vehicle, Ars interviewed Kirk Shireman, Human Spaceflight Exploration and Orion program manager at Lockheed Martin.
summary: NASA's Artemis program changes allow SpaceX Starship and Blue Origin Blue Moon to dock with Orion in Earth orbit and low‑lunar orbit, respectively. These adjustments ease lander operations but increase the load on Orion, built by Lockheed Martin, according to program manager Kirk Shireman.
author: Ars Technica

title: Meta’s AI agent Muse mixes up conversations and may expose private data
content: A report claims Meta’s AI agent Muse is mixing up conversations and could be exposing private data. Employees said Muse surfaced messages about childcare requests they never made, career advice they never asked for, product orders they never placed, and bank account balances that did not belong to them.
summary: Employees reported that Meta’s AI agent Muse displayed messages about childcare requests they never made. The agent also showed career advice they never asked for, product orders they never placed, and bank account balances that did not belong to them.
author: TechCrunch

title: Fireworks AI Co-Founder Advocates Open-Source Models After Anthropic Goes Public
content: On the day Anthropic went public, Fireworks AI’s co‑founder argued that companies could largely avoid expensive models by using open‑source alternatives. He also discussed data breaches that eroded some customers’ trust in the company.
summary: Fireworks AI’s co-founder argued that open source models are a cheaper alternative to pricey AI models. He also addressed breaches that have cost the company some customers’ trust.
author: TechCrunch

title: 15 Tips for Playing Grand Theft Auto VI, Including Fast Walk Setting
content: There’s a vast amount to absorb in Leonida, but these pointers will rev up your criminal engines and allow you to better enjoy the ride Tell us: are you playing Grand Theft Auto VI? Leonida is so huge as to be overwhelming and in the opening hours, the game bombards you with tonnes of info that you will inevitably forget. But I’ve done nothing but play this game for weeks and I’m here to help. Here’s what I wished I’d known at the start Walk faster. I found that Jason and Lucia walk incredibly slowly. If you go into the options menu, you can select “fast walk” as the default walking speed, which sped them up just a little without ruining the pace or atmosphere of the game. While you’re in there, you can also customise plenty of other things, including controls and button mapping.
summary: The article provides 15 tips for navigating the large city of Leonida in Grand Theft Auto VI. One tip advises enabling the “fast walk” option to increase Jason and Lucia’s walking speed and notes that the options menu also allows customization of controls and button mapping.
author: Guardian Technology

title: Parents urged not to buy GTA VI for children due to explicit 18+ content
content:
