title: Ireland's Prendergast cleared to face South Africa after hip-drop tackle ban dismissed
content:
Ireland fly-half Sam Prendergast will face South Africa in the Nations Championship on Saturday after an independent disciplinary committee dismissed his citation for an alleged hip-drop tackle. The 23-year-old was originally cited for a challenge on Fiji captain Peceli Yato, an offense under Law 9.13 introduced in November. Following a hearing on Tuesday, the committee decided no further action would be taken, sparing Prendergast a potential suspension.

South Africa Rugby also condemned online abuse directed at officials, while coach Rassie Erasmus had previously predicted the player would be cleared.
summary: Ireland's fly-half Sam Prendergast is available to face South Africa in the Nations Championship after an independent disciplinary committee dismissed his citation for an alleged hip-drop tackle. The 23-year-old was cited for a challenge against Fiji's captain Peceli Yato, but the committee decided no further action would be taken.
author: Guardian Sport

title: MLB Commissioner Manfred Says Owners Will Not Budge on Salary Cap, Lockout Looms
content: 2027 season under threat amid dispute over salary cap Commissioner says fans want a more equal game MLB commissioner, Rob Manfred, has insisted owners will not budge from their demand for a salary cap, leaving the league on track for a lockout starting 2 December that could threaten the 2027 season. “I can’t imagine the owners ratifying a deal that does not include a cap and floor,” Manfred said on Wednesday at a news conference during an owners meeting. Players say they will never accept a cap. The last time management proposed a cap in 1994, it led to a strike that lasted almost eight months and caused the cancellation of the World Series for the first time in 90 years.
summary: MLB Commissioner Rob Manfred stated that owners will not accept a deal without a salary cap and floor, putting the league on track for a lockout starting December 2. Players have rejected the cap concept, and the dispute threatens the 2027 season amid a history of labor conflicts.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Emma Hayes to assist US Soccer in search for next USMNT coach
content:
US women’s national team head coach Emma Hayes has confirmed her participation in the search for the next USMNT manager. Speaking after announcing her squad for the Concacaf championship and World Cup qualifier, Hayes stated she is confident in the group assembled to select Mauricio Pochettino’s replacement. Pochettino recently departed for Manchester United.

The selection committee includes Hayes, US Soccer CEO JT Batson, chief operating officer Dan Helfrich, and vice-president of sporting Oguchi Onyewu. Hayes, who won the 2024 Olympics and enjoyed a trophy-laden tenure at Chelsea, shed light on her role in this hiring process for the first time.
summary: US women’s national team head coach Emma Hayes said she is confident in the group selected to find a replacement for Mauricio Pochettino. The search team includes US Soccer CEO JT Batson, chief operating officer Dan Helfrich, and vice-president of sporting Oguchi Onyewu.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Leicester City ends BC Game sponsorship after porn actor partnership
content:
Leicester City has terminated its front-of-shirt sponsorship agreement with BC Game, an offshore cryptocurrency casino registered in Belize that is unlicensed to operate in the UK. The club, which had partnered with the betting firm since 2024, cited “differing commercial priorities” as the reason for prematurely ending the deal on Wednesday.

The decision followed a fan backlash triggered when BC Game named Eva Elfie, a porn actor, as a brand ambassador this month. In response to the partnership, the Foxes Trust, Leicester’s supporters’ trust, highlighted the “devastating impacts” associated with gambling and pornography.
summary: Leicester City terminated its front-of-shirt sponsorship deal with cryptocurrency casino BC Game following a fan backlash over the company's partnership with Eva Elfie. The club cited differing commercial priorities for the early end to the agreement, which had been in place since 2024.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Veerle Buurman scores late winner as Chelsea beat PSG in WCL
content:
Veerle Buurman scored a late winner to help Chelsea edge past Paris Saint-Germain in a Champions League match. The goal secured three points for Chelsea, who struggled to break down a resilient PSG defense. The victory temporarily placed Chelsea at the top of the league phase table.

Buurman continued her strong form following a standout performance against Manchester City earlier that weekend, where she came on as a substitute and was named player of the match. In the match against PSG, she was the decisive factor, finding the net at the near post after Chelsea created numerous chances without scoring.
summary: Veerle Buurman scored a late goal to help Chelsea defeat Paris Saint-Germain in the Champions League. The victory temporarily places Chelsea at the top of the league phase table.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Rugby brain injury lawsuits at collapse risk after document disclosure delays
content:
Rugby brain injury lawsuits involving hundreds of players are nearing collapse due to repeated delays in disclosing medical documents. Lead counsel Paul Downes KC conceded in June that the claimants were in the “last-chance saloon” after missing court-mandated deadlines, a situation that has worsened following another failure to meet requirements in October. The legal team is now arguing for an extension until January to prevent the cases from failing.

The future of these six-year-old, high-cost legal battles rests on upcoming decisions by two judges. The claimants’ consistent failure to disclose documents to the defendants has placed the proceedings on the brink of termination, with the current status described as being beyond the previous “last-chance” warning.
summary: The lead counsel for the claimants has conceded that the lawsuits are in the "last-chance saloon" after repeatedly missing court-mandated deadlines for document disclosure. The future of the case now rests on the decisions of two judges following the claimants' failure to meet a deadline in October.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Manchester United's 1974 relegation offers warning for current decline
content:
Manchester United’s current relegation zone position, its first in 40 years, draws striking parallels to the club’s 1974 relegation. The article highlights similarities in both eras, including the departure of a legendary manager whose shadow remained, alongside boardroom uncertainty and the rapid turnover of replacements.

Sir Matt Busby stepped aside as manager of the 1968 European Cup-winning side but stayed on as a director. This mirrors the situation with Sir Alex Ferguson, who watched from the Old Trafford directors’ box as his successors tried and failed, leading to the club’s slide over several years.
summary: The article highlights striking parallels between Manchester United's 1974 relegation and the club's current presence in the relegation zone for the first time in 40 years. It notes that in both eras, a legendary manager departed while remaining a director, leading to boardroom uncertainty and a succession of failed replacements.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Cameron Bancroft exposes details of 2018 Australian cricket cheating scandal
content: The time for formal measures has passed but all involved have betrayed the trust of a country whose Test team is sacred Cry havoc. But Cameron Bancroft did not let anything slip, not after close to a decade of keeping his mouth firmly shut. It was a deliberate, considered and lengthy deed of revelation that the former Test opening bat chose to publish in the West Australian newspaper on Wednesday, claiming to finally fill in a wealth of detail around Australian cricket’s 2018 cheating scandal that so many others seem to have gone to such lengths to keep concealed. It was also a devastating repudiation of Pat Cummins, a teammate of equivalent juniority to Bancroft during their few months playing together, but now the Test captain, who had delivered his own manifesto in spoken form at a press conference last week. That version of events, in which Cummins was adamant that he had never been aware of any kind of ball-tampering in Australian colours, was what pushed Bancroft from silence to speech. “It made me feel angry, betrayed and alone,” Bancroft wrote. “What I saw, experienced and lived with not only him, but everyone else on that tour in South Africa is not the public account he gave in his press conference and in the years previously.”
summary: Former Test opening bat Cameron Bancroft published a detailed account of the 2018 Australian cricket cheating scandal in the West Australian newspaper on Wednesday. His revelations repudiated Test captain Pat Cummins, who had denied any knowledge of ball‑tampering during a press conference last week.
author: Guardian Sport

content: Veerle Buurman netted an 87th‑minute goal to give Chelsea a 1‑0 victory over Paris St‑Germain in the Women’s Champions League, moving the English side to the top of the group table. The late winner secured Chelsea’s edge in the match.
